title: The Final Experiment

beats.narrativeText: Atlas reveals that one experiment remains unfinished.
Unlike every previous investigation, no detailed instructions for this experiment survive.
The learner must define the investigation and form a prediction using everything learned throughout the campaign.
Planning a fair test reveals just how much independent reasoning this final investigation requires.
The learner must collect evidence and analyse the results without step-by-step guidance.
The learner successfully completes the expedition's final, unfinished investigation.
The learner reflects on the limitations of their investigation and what could be improved.
Confidence shifts from following procedures to designing them — the learner is no longer just completing investigations, but planning their own.

activities.title: Define the Investigation
activities.storyContext: One experiment remains unfinished, and no detailed instructions survive for it.
activities.instructions: Decide exactly what question your investigation will try to answer.

activities.title: Form a Prediction
activities.storyContext: A good investigation starts with a prediction to test.
activities.instructions: Form a prediction for what you expect your investigation to show, and explain your reasoning.

activities.title: Plan a Fair Test
activities.storyContext: Atlas provides only safety guidance and procedural reminders — the design is up to the learner.
activities.instructions: Plan a fair test for your investigation, changing only one thing at a time.
activities.output: A plan for a fair test.

activities.title: Collect Evidence
activities.storyContext: Every conclusion needs evidence to support it.
activities.instructions: Carry out your fair test and collect evidence carefully.

activities.title: Analyse Results
activities.storyContext: The evidence must be analysed to see whether it supports the original prediction.
activities.instructions: Analyse your results and decide whether they support your prediction.
activities.output: An analysis of the investigation's results.

activities.title: Reflect on Limitations
activities.storyContext: No investigation is ever completely perfect.
activities.instructions: Reflect on the limitations of your investigation and what you would improve.
activities.output: A reflection on the investigation's limitations.

activities.title: Repeat With a Changed Variable
activities.storyContext: Changing one variable can reveal whether your first result was reliable.
activities.instructions: Repeat your investigation with one variable changed, and compare the outcomes.
activities.output: A comparison between the original and repeated investigation.

activities.title: Is Experimental Evidence Reliable?
activities.storyContext: Deciding whether evidence is trustworthy is a core scientific skill.
activities.instructions: Find out how scientists decide whether experimental evidence is reliable.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What would you do differently if you repeated your investigation?

discussionPoints: How did you decide what to test, with no instructions to follow?
What would you do differently if you repeated this investigation?
parentGuide.preparation: Materials will depend on what the learner chooses to investigate — encourage them to plan first, then gather what they need.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a genuinely fair test (only one thing changed at a time) and honest reflection on the investigation's limitations.

completionCriteria: An investigation defined, a fair test planned, evidence collected, and results analysed.
